title: Count the Nodes

concept.title: Count the root, then count both subtrees
body: Many questions about a tree are answered by one pattern: **solve the question for the left subtree, solve it for the right subtree, and combine the two answers with the root**. The questions about the empty tree are the base case.
For counting nodes the combination is a sum: the tree has one node (the root) plus all nodes of the left subtree plus all nodes of the right subtree.

Each node is visited exactly once, so the time is proportional to the number of nodes. The recursion goes as deep as the tree is high, which is why the trees of this topic are limited to a height of 800 (Python allows about 1000 nested calls).

statement: Print the number of nodes of a binary tree.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
hints: The empty tree has no nodes.
Count the root as 1 and add the sizes of the left and the right subtree.
The input already tells you nothing more: just walk the tree.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root

    if root is None:
        print("empty")

        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def count(root):
    if root is None:
        return 0
